where: Section 2, bullet on the buffer and synchronisation stage
problem: "It absorbs jitter and inserts or drops timing" is unclear and technically loose. A buffer cannot insert or drop timing. It inserts extra delay and drops (or repeats) frames, samples or packets.
fix: "It absorbs jitter by adding a small delay, and it drops or repeats frames and samples when a stream runs ahead or behind, so that audio and video stay on one timeline."

where: Lead versus Exam traps, third bullet
problem: The lead says the stages are "joined by a common clock", while the trap says audio and video "have independent clocks". Read together, a student may think the two statements contradict.
fix: In the lead, say the streams are "aligned to one presentation clock". In the trap, say "audio and video are captured on their own sample and frame clocks; the buffer aligns them to a single presentation clock. Their bit rates are independent."

where: Figure and Section 2 list (ordering of buffer, storage and network)
problem: The pipeline draws buffer and sync before storage and network, but the text says the buffer absorbs jitter from storage and the network. On playback (set-top box, phone call) the playout buffer sits after the network and storage, just before presentation. A student drawing the receive path from this figure will put the buffer in the wrong place.
fix: Add one sentence: in the capture path the buffer sits after the codec; in the playback path the same stage sits between the network or file system and the decoder, so network jitter is absorbed before playout.

problem: The percentage is truncated, not rounded. 1,411,200 ÷ 222,595,200 × 100 = 0.633976%, which rounds to 0.6340%, not 0.6339%.
